company_items.summary: A flood of post-Friday-close headlines hit Anthropic hard. The IPO is being pushed to November from October, year-end ARR projections came in at greater than 100 to 110 billion dollars versus bull hopes of 120 billion dollars or more, and the company is targeting a 100 billion dollar-plus raise at a greater than 2 trillion dollar valuation. OpenAI's Astra launch has taken momentum, though Anthropic may release a new model pre-IPO to recapture ground. Anthropic also disclosed plans for 5 gigawatts of compute by year-end doubling to 10 gigawatts by end of 2027.

Oracle was the subject of a negative Financial Times article Friday focused on poor price action in debt tied to a massive Oracle-linked data center in New Mexico known as Project Jupiter. Efforts to offload loans tied to the facility have reportedly hit a wall, raising concerns about the company's off-balance sheet data center financing exposure.

Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California to resolve a state attorney general lawsuit against its merger with Warner Bros Discovery. The settlement could require Paramount to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest certain cable channels including Comedy Central. Resolution of this overhang could help the Warner deal move forward.

Paramount's advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general over the Warner deal could include divesting cable channels like Comedy Central and preserving CNN's editorial independence. A settlement removes a key regulatory obstacle to closing the merger. The outcome remains uncertain but progress is incrementally positive for deal completion.

Wendy's saw pressure Friday after one of its largest franchisees, Meritage Hospitality Group, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. This raises concerns about franchisee financial health and the broader consumer spending environment for quick-service restaurants.

Novo Nordisk is being pressured by shareholders to diversify away from GLP-1 exposure through mergers and acquisitions. The pressure reflects investor concern about concentration risk in the GLP-1 franchise and a desire for the company to deploy capital more broadly.

Boeing is in talks with NASA for its Starliner capsule to be used on ten or more new flights into low-Earth orbit, a potential significant contract win that could rehabilitate the program following its troubled history. This would represent meaningful new revenue and a reputational boost for Boeing's space division.

Accenture will embed a team of evaluators to monitor safety and alignment at Anthropic, a contract that positions the firm at the center of the growing AI governance and oversight industry. The announcement came Friday night alongside broader news about Anthropic's IPO preparations.

Volkswagen issued a large downside preannouncement Friday for 2026 operating margins, now guiding to up to 1% versus the Street's roughly 4.1% estimate and prior guidance of 4 to 5.5%. The miss is driven by a goodwill impairment charge at Porsche, a challenging auto market especially in China, and additional restructuring expenses. Adjusted for special items operating margins would be roughly 4%, essentially inline with consensus.

Kroger is dropping Red Bull from its stores as the grocery giant pushes back against supplier price hikes. The move signals intensifying retailer leverage over consumer packaged goods suppliers and growing consumer price sensitivity in discretionary beverage categories.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your market setup for the week of September 21st, 2026.

The weekend brought net negative news flow on two major fronts: the Middle East and artificial intelligence. On geopolitics, the Houthis in Yemen dramatically escalated attacks on major Saudi Arabian cities over the weekend, setting fuel depots ablaze and demonstrating that the Iran-aligned group is willing to target critical infrastructure. The Pentagon is stretched thin escorting tankers through the Strait of Hormuz and lacks the bandwidth to respond to multiplying threats. Iran separately warned that any resumed US military action would trigger a fierce response. Ukraine also launched a massive drone strike on Russia including Moscow. The bottom line is the Iran war continues to metastasize and energy markets remain under serious pressure, with the diesel and motor oil shortages in the US directly tied to this conflict.

On artificial intelligence, a wave of negative headlines broke after Friday's close. Anthropic's IPO is being pushed from October to November. Year-end annual recurring revenue projections came in at over 100 to 110 billion dollars, below bull expectations of 120 billion or more. OpenAI disclosed it expects negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars between 2026 and 2030 as spending dramatically outpaces revenue. And the Financial Times reported that Big Tech's off-balance sheet artificial intelligence liability exposure has risen roughly 300 billion dollars in just the last twelve months. Oracle was also hit by a negative report about debt tied to its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, with efforts to offload those loans described as having hit a wall.

On individual names, Wendy's is under pressure after one of its largest franchisees filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Volkswagen issued a major profit warning, cutting its 2026 operating margin guidance to up to 1% from prior guidance of 4 to 5.5%, blaming Porsche impairment charges, China weakness, and restructuring costs. Kroger is dropping Red Bull from its stores as it pushes back on supplier pricing. On the positive side, Boeing is in talks with NASA for Starliner to fly ten or more new low-Earth orbit missions, a meaningful potential contract win for a program that badly needs rehabilitation.

For macro catalysts this week, the two biggest are the US flash PMIs on Wednesday morning and the Trump-Xi summit on Thursday. The summit could produce modest tariff reductions on roughly 30 billion dollars of goods and potentially eliminate Chinese tariffs on US liquefied natural gas. The UN General Assembly runs through September 28th and brings Iranian officials to New York, creating at least a theoretical opening for diplomatic progress on the Middle East — though Adam is skeptical a breakthrough occurs.

Monetary policy globally remains hawkish. The Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan all hiked this month. Markets are now pricing greater than 50% odds of additional hikes from multiple central banks over the next several weeks. Kansas City Fed President Schmid warned Friday that inflation is running too hot even without oil, reinforcing the higher-for-longer message.

The directional lean going into Monday is cautious to bearish. The weekend news flow adds pressure to an already complex tape. Watch oil prices at the open, any diplomatic signals from the UN General Assembly, and Anthropic-linked names for sentiment on the broader artificial intelligence trade. Stay nimble.
